paper.title: Improved Regret Bounds for Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound in Bayesian Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian optimization (Bayesian setting of GP bandit)
unmapped: Domain is [0,r]^d; f is a sample path of a known zero-mean GP with kernel k(x,x) <= 1 (SE or Matern)
Learner knows the sample-path Lipschitz constants a, b (Lemma 1) and r, used in beta_t
settings.definition_quote: Let $f: \mX \rightarrow \R$ be a black-box objective function whose input domain $\mX$ is $\mX \coloneqq [0, r]^d$ ... We consider a Bayesian setting, where the objective function $f$ and the noise sequence $(\epsilon_t)$ are drawn from a known zero-mean Gaussian process (GP) and a Gaussian distribution, respectively. ... the cumulative regret $R_T \coloneqq \sum_{t \in [T]} f(\bx^{\ast}) - f(\bx_t)$

symbols.delta_GP: failure probability for the sample-path regularity properties of Lemma 2

conditions: Matern kernel with smoothness nu_matern > 2 and 2*nu_matern + d <= nu_matern^2
d, nu, lengthscale ell, r, sigma^2 are fixed constants
f ~ GP(0,k) on [0,r]^d, Gaussian noise N(0, sigma^2)
holds with probability at least 1 - delta_GP - delta; hidden constants depend on ln(1/delta), d, nu, ell, r, sigma^2 and sample-path constants c_sup, c_gap, rho_quad, c_quad associated with delta_GP
tuning: beta_t = 2 ln(2 t^2 pi^2/(3 delta)) + 2d ln(t^2 d b r sqrt(ln(4da/delta))) with delta in (0, 1 - delta_GP)
